{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Bernoulli best-arm identification: fixed confidence and expected stopping cost\par}\vspace{5pt}
\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{ON\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}FC\_\allowbreak{}\allowbreak{}S}

Online learning and bandits

The algorithm adaptively samples Bernoulli arms, chooses a stopping time, and recommends the unique best arm. It must attain the prescribed confidence for every admissible mean vector. Cost is the expected number of samples on the instance; the central comparison concerns the leading constant as confidence tends to one for a fixed instance.

\textbf{Status.} Fully optimal

\textbf{TASK tags.} formulation: Best arm fixed confidence; solution concept: Minimize expected stopping time; task family: Online bandit

\textbf{MODEL tags.} stochastic model: Parametric bernoulli; structure: Finite actions; structure: Unique best

\textbf{ORACLE tags.} feedback quality: Source-declared exact feedback (may be a random reward); interface family: Selected reward; operation: Sample selected arm; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared

\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} randomization: Private randomness allowed

\textbf{OUTPUT tags.} certificate: No additional output certificate required; object: Stopping time and arm recommendation

\textbf{METRIC tags.} criterion: Uniform fixed-confidence identification correctness

\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} confidence: Confidence parameter explicitly declared; mode: Uniform fixed-confidence identification correctness; randomness: Algorithm private seed; randomness: Oracle samples

\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} accounting: Joint coordinates retained; budget: Instancewise expected stopping cost (not a worst-instance supremum); measure: Samples; measure: Stopping checks

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}
The algorithm adaptively samples Bernoulli arms, chooses a stopping time, and recommends the unique best arm. It must attain the prescribed confidence for every admissible mean vector. Cost is the expected number of samples on the instance; the central comparison concerns the leading constant as confidence tends to one for a fixed instance.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}
The fixed unknown mean vector satisfies \AtlasInlineMath{\mu\in(0,1)^K} and has a unique best arm. Both means and individual arm gaps are hidden.

The data-dependent stopping time \AtlasInlineMath{\tau_\delta} is measurable with respect to observed history and is not a fixed horizon.

The arm \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat{b}} is recommended at stopping. Correctness must hold uniformly over all admissible mean vectors.

The comparison characteristic time \AtlasInlineMath{T^*(\mu)} is defined by the allocation problem using forward \AtlasInlineMath{\operatorname{KL}(\nu_{\mu_i}\,\|\,\nu_{\lambda_i})}. It is an analytical benchmark, not an input supplied to the algorithm.

The full characteristic time \AtlasInlineMath{T^*(\mu)} is defined by \AtlasInlineMath{T^*(\mu)^{-1}=\sup_{w\in\Delta_K}\inf_{\lambda\in\operatorname{Alt}(\mu)}\sum_i w_i\operatorname{kl}(\mu_i,\lambda_i)}. The alternative class, Bernoulli KL divergence, and simplex are defined in the local notation table.

Require \AtlasInlineMath{K\ge2} and \AtlasInlineMath{0<\delta<1/2}. Both round actions and the final recommendation lie in \AtlasInlineMath{[K]}.

Take delta to zero with the instance mu fixed. Finite-parameter conclusions in which K or mu also vary are not part of this leading-constant comparison.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}
Bernoulli arm sampling:


\AtlasMath{a_t\in[K],\quad t\le\tau_\delta\ \longmapsto\ Y_t\in\{0,1\},\quad \mathbb{P}(Y_t=1\mid\mathcal{H}_{t-1},a_t)=\mu_{a_t}}


Each call returns a fresh independent Bernoulli sample.

Arm choices depend only on the history; stopping and recommendation use information already obtained.

No extra samples are taken after stopping. This task has no regret-bearing action point.

Public inputs are K, $\delta$, and the Bernoulli family. The means $\mu$ and gaps are hidden.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}
Output an almost surely finite stopping time \AtlasInlineMath{\tau_\delta} and recommended arm \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat{b}\in[K]}. A computable correctness certificate is not required. No samples may be drawn after stopping.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}

\AtlasMath{p_\mu(\mathcal{A}_\delta)=\Pr_\mu(\widehat{b}\ne b(\mu)),\qquad C_\mu(\mathcal{A}_\delta)=\mathbb{E}_\mu[\tau_\delta].}


The identification loss is an error indicator, and expected stopping time is the cost. The asymptotic efficiency quantity \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{E}_\mu[\tau_\delta]/\log(1/\delta)} is kept distinct from fixed-budget error probability.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}
Each arm pull yields one charged sample. The total number of samples is the random stopping time \AtlasInlineMath{\tau_\delta}, and the primary resource objective is the instancewise expectation \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{E}_\mu[\tau_\delta]}.

Any causal randomized algorithm that is uniformly delta-correct is allowed.

Track-and-Stop maintains empirical means, sample counts, and likelihood ratios and numerically computes allocation proportions. Those computations are not identified with one sample at no additional accounting cost.

Information calls, arithmetic, communication rounds, and memory are measured separately. Exact real internal computation is excluded from information complexity unless explicitly charged. This does not imply a bit-complexity bound.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}
Arbitrary causal randomized sampling, stopping, and recommendation rules are allowed. The algorithm must achieve the confidence guarantee uniformly over all admissible mean vectors and stop almost surely. Internal computation and storage are unrestricted.

One algorithm family \AtlasInlineMath{\{\mathcal{A}_\delta\}} must satisfy \AtlasInlineMath{\Pr_\mu(\widehat{b}=b(\mu))\ge1-\delta} for every admissible mean vector \AtlasInlineMath{\mu} and stop almost surely. Expected-cost guarantees are instancewise. In the limit \AtlasInlineMath{\delta\downarrow0}, hold \AtlasInlineMath{K} and the entire \AtlasInlineMath{\mu} fixed. Randomness includes sampling and the algorithm.

\textbf{Budget convention.} The sample count \AtlasInlineMath{\tau_\delta} is random, with primary cost \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb E_\mu\tau_\delta}. There is no prespecified hard budget \AtlasInlineMath{T}.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}
\AtlasInlineMath{K}: The finite number of arms. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{K\in\mathbb N,\ K\ge2}.

The arm set is \AtlasInlineMath{[K]=\{1,\ldots,K\}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\delta}: The allowed statistical failure probability. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<\delta<1/2}.

Used only for statistical correctness or high-probability performance, and distinct from the privacy relaxation parameter.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mu}: Unknown Bernoulli mean vector \textbf{Domain:} The vector \AtlasInlineMath{\mu\in(0,1)^K} has a unique largest component.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mu_i=\mathbb E_{Y\sim\nu_i}Y}, where \AtlasInlineMath{\nu_i=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\mu_i)}.

\AtlasInlineMath{[K]}: Index set of K arms or experts \textbf{Domain:} A finite set.

\AtlasInlineMath{[K]=\{1,\ldots,K\}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal M_K}: Class of Bernoulli mean vectors with a unique best arm \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal M_K\subset(0,1)^K}.

The instance class is \AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal M_K=\{\mu\in(0,1)^K:\arg\max_i\mu_i\text{ contains exactly one arm}\}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{b(\mu)}: Unique best arm of mean vector mu \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{b(\mu)\in[K]}.

\AtlasInlineMath{b(\mu)=\arg\max_i\mu_i}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\tau_\delta}: A stopping time determined by observed data. \textbf{Domain:} A nonnegative integer-valued stopping time.

The quantity \AtlasInlineMath{\mu\in\mathcal M_K} is almost surely finite on every admissible instance. Its expectation is the charged sampling cost.

\AtlasInlineMath{\widehat b_{\tau_\delta}}: Arm recommended upon stopping \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat b_{\tau_\delta}\in[K]}.

The guarantee \AtlasInlineMath{\Pr_\mu(\widehat b_{\tau_\delta}\ne b(\mu))\le\delta} holds for every admissible mu.

\AtlasInlineMath{\operatorname{Alt}(\mu)}: Alternative mean vectors with a different best arm. \textbf{Domain:} The set of mean vectors.

The expression is \AtlasInlineMath{\{\lambda\in\mathcal M_K:b(\lambda)\ne b(\mu)\}}; taking the closure in the inner infimum gives an equivalent value.

\AtlasInlineMath{\operatorname{kl}(p,q)}: Forward relative entropy of Bernoulli distributions. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{p,q\in(0,1)}.

The expression is \AtlasInlineMath{p\log(p/q)+(1-p)\log((1-p)/(1-q))}, with endpoints defined by continuous limits.

\AtlasInlineMath{\Delta_K,w}: The sampling-proportion simplex and its elements. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{w\in\Delta_K}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\Delta_K=\{w\in[0,1]^K:\sum_iw_i=1\}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\lambda}: Alternative means in the inner characteristic-time optimization. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\lambda\in\operatorname{Alt}(\mu)}.

\AtlasInlineMath{T^*(\mu)}: Instance characteristic time for fixed-confidence identification \textbf{Domain:} Positive real number used only in analysis of the hidden instance.


\AtlasMath{T^*(\mu)^{-1}=\sup_{w\in\Delta_K}\inf_{\lambda\in\operatorname{Alt}(\mu)}\sum_iw_i\operatorname{kl}(\mu_i,\lambda_i)}
.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal T_\delta(\mu)}: Minimum expected sample count among all uniformly delta-correct algorithms that stop almost surely \textbf{Domain:} A nonnegative real.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal T_\delta(\mu)=\inf_{\mathcal A\ \delta\text{correct}}\mathbb E_\mu\tau_\delta}. The algorithm must first be uniformly correct; its performance is then evaluated at the fixed instance $\mu$.

\AtlasInlineMath{\beta(t,\delta)}: Public threshold in the Chernoff stopping rule \textbf{Domain:} Real number.

\AtlasInlineMath{\beta(t,\delta)=\log(2(K-1)t/\delta)}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\widehat\mu,w^*(\widehat\mu)}: Empirical arm means and their characteristic-time-optimal allocation. \textbf{Domain:} Algorithm's internal statistic.

The vector \AtlasInlineMath{w^*} is an optimal sampling proportion in the outer maximization defining characteristic time. It cannot be computed using the hidden true mu as an input.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal A}: Learning policies satisfying the specified information, computation, and privacy restrictions \textbf{Domain:} A measurable causal policy.

Actions may depend only on revealed information and the private seed. Additional restrictions are governed by the algorithm protocol in this profile.

\AtlasInlineMath{t}: Interaction-time index \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{t\in\mathbb N,\ t\ge1}.

Sampling time. The data-dependent stopping time \AtlasInlineMath{\tau_\delta} has no prespecified horizon \AtlasInlineMath{T}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb E}: Mean operator \textbf{Domain:} Expectation over the specified random variables.

Expectation includes learner randomness and the explicitly specified reward or sample randomness. Conditional expectations retain their stated history conditioning.

\AtlasInlineMath{\log,\log_2}: Natural and binary logarithms \textbf{Domain:} Function on the positive real axis.

\AtlasInlineMath{\log x=\ln x}, \AtlasInlineMath{\log_2x=\log x/\log2}.

\AtlasInlineMath{c,C}: Positive constant in the bound without an assigned numerical value \textbf{Domain:} Positive real number.

Constants apply only under the associated bound’s conditions and fixed-parameter convention. Unspecified theorem constants are not treated as additional algorithm inputs.

\AtlasInlineMath{O,\Omega,\widetilde O,\widetilde\Omega}: Asymptotic upper and lower bounds, including explicitly permitted logarithmic suppression. \textbf{Domain:} Asymptotic comparison notation.

The result applies only in the regime declared for that bound. Tilde notation hides only its stated logarithms and fixed-parameter dependencies, never additional polynomial parameter factors.

\AtlasInlineMath{N}: Cumulative observations counted according to the declared feedback type. \textbf{Domain:} Nonnegative integer or integer-valued stopping time.

The quantity \AtlasInlineMath{N=\tau_\delta} is the cumulative number of scalar reward samples before stopping.

\needspace{12\baselineskip}\section{3. Complexity bracket}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Compared quantities}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Q1 - asymptotic expected sample constant}
\AtlasMath{\begin{aligned} C_{\rm FC}(\mu)&=\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\inf_{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_\delta}\frac{\mathbb E_{\mu,\mathcal A}[\tau_\delta]}{\log(1/\delta)},\qquad \mu,K\ \text{fixed},\\ \mathfrak A_\delta&=\{\mathcal A:\ \forall\lambda\in\mathcal M_K,\ \mathbb P_{\lambda,\mathcal A}(\tau_\delta<\infty)=1,\\ &\hspace{5em}\mathbb P_{\lambda,\mathcal A}(\widehat b_{\tau_\delta}\ne b(\lambda))\le\delta\},\\ \mathcal M_K&=\{\mu\in(0,1)^K:\ b(\mu)\text{ is unique}\}.\end{aligned}}
\textbf{Scope.} Compare only this specification and the listed parameter regions.

\textbf{Optimization direction.} minimize

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{R1 - ASYMPTOTIC}
\textbf{Region.} Fix a mean vector mu with a unique best arm and arm count K, then take delta to zero.

\textbf{Quantity.} Q1

\textbf{Resource.} Native sequential interaction rounds or samples; additional resources remain attached to each bound.

\textbf{Status.} Optimal

\textbf{Lower bound.} B2

\AtlasMath{T*(\mu )}
\textbf{Upper bound.} B1

\AtlasMath{T*(\mu )}
\textbf{Gap or comparison.} The same leading asymptotic constant when \AtlasInlineMath{\mu} and \AtlasInlineMath{K} are fixed.

\textbf{Comparison argument.} Only individually audited compatible claims enter. No inversion into fixed-budget exponent; its KL orientation and quantifiers differ.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{4. Bounds and supporting evidence}
The following conditions apply to every bound in this profile, in addition to each bound's stated region and algorithm scope.

\textbf{Conditions.} Fix the arm count \AtlasInlineMath{K} and mean vector \AtlasInlineMath{\mu} with a unique best arm, and consider \AtlasInlineMath{\delta\to0}. The confidence requirement holds on every admissible instance, not merely one known instance.

\textbf{Dimension conditions.} Dimension, arm count, and horizon must satisfy the stated region. Large-dimension and asymptotic source conditions are retained.

\textbf{Oracle mapping.} Preserve current-round feedback content, response timing, and sample coupling, without adding access to hidden objects.

\textbf{Guarantee mapping.} Retain this setting's cumulative regret, error probability, stopping time, or error exponent, including the order of aggregation. Required conversions are stated in the bound's derivation.

\textbf{Output mapping.} Use the actual action trajectory or terminal recommendation required by the specification. Post-hoc averaging is allowed only where an explicit derivation justifies that transfer.

\textbf{Resource mapping.} Native queries and initialization use the declared resource units. No extra samples or revisits to past rounds are free.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{B1 - Track-and-Stop with C-/D-tracking and Bernoulli Chernoff threshold}
\textbf{Admission.} Included in the bracket

\textbf{Direction.} upper

\textbf{Witness or lower-bound scope.} Deterministic witness

\AtlasMath{\limsup_{\delta\downarrow0}\frac{\mathbb{E}_\mu[\tau_\delta]}{\log(1/\delta)}\le T^*(\mu)}
\textbf{Sources.} \href{https://proceedings.mlr.press/v49/garivier16a.pdf}{[1]}

\textbf{Simultaneous resource costs.} All coordinates refer to this one witness or necessary constraint.

\textbf{samples.}

\AtlasMath{E_mu \tau}
\textbf{stopping checks.}

\AtlasMath{\le \tau}
\textbf{Constants.} Universal constants independent of the parameters explicitly tracked in this claim

\textbf{Logarithmic factors.} None.

\textbf{Source location.} \href{https://proceedings.mlr.press/v49/garivier16a.pdf}{[1]} pdf pages: 10; 13; theorem: Theorems 10 and 14

For Bernoulli rewards, use Chernoff stopping threshold \AtlasInlineMath{\log(2(K-1)t/\delta)} with C- or D-tracking. The source choice \AtlasInlineMath{\alpha=1} yields asymptotic expected-sample constant \AtlasInlineMath{T^\star(\mu)}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{B2 - Change of measure across $Alt(\mu )$}
\textbf{Admission.} Included in the bracket

\textbf{Direction.} lower

\textbf{Witness or lower-bound scope.} All randomized adaptive algorithms

\AtlasMath{\begin{aligned}[c]\mathbb{E}_\mu[\tau_\delta]&\ge T^*(\mu)\operatorname{kl}(\delta,1-\delta),\\ \liminf_{\delta\downarrow0}\frac{\mathbb{E}_\mu[\tau_\delta]}{\log(1/\delta)}&\ge T^*(\mu),\\ T^*(\mu)^{-1}&=\sup_{w\in\Delta_K}\inf_{\lambda\in\operatorname{Alt}(\mu)}\sum_{i=1}^K w_i\operatorname{kl}(\mu_i,\lambda_i).\end{aligned}}
\textbf{Sources.} \href{https://proceedings.mlr.press/v49/garivier16a.pdf}{[1]}

\textbf{Simultaneous resource costs.} All coordinates refer to this one witness or necessary constraint.

\textbf{samples.}

\AtlasMath{E_mu \tau}
\textbf{Constants.} Universal constants independent of the parameters explicitly tracked in this claim

\textbf{Logarithmic factors.} None.

\textbf{Derivation.} Fix the number of arms and a mean vector with a unique best arm, and let \AtlasInlineMath{\delta\to0}. The binary relative entropy satisfies \AtlasInlineMath{\operatorname{kl}(\delta,1-\delta)/\log(1/\delta)\to1}, giving the asymptotic sample constant. No uniform statement is made when arm gaps shrink simultaneously.

\textbf{Source location.} \href{https://proceedings.mlr.press/v49/garivier16a.pdf}{[1]} pdf pages: 3; 4; theorem: Theorem 1

Every policy that is \AtlasInlineMath{\delta}-PAC on the entire admissible instance class satisfies \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb E_\mu\tau\ge T^\star(\mu)\operatorname{kl}(\delta,1-\delta)}. The characteristic time uses the forward divergence \AtlasInlineMath{\operatorname{KL}(\mu_i,\lambda_i)}.

For each fixed finite K>=\allowbreak{}2 and fixed mu in (0,\allowbreak{}1)\textasciicircum{}K with a unique largest coordinate,\allowbreak{} take delta down to 0 through 0<delta<1/\allowbreak{}2. There is no worst-case-over-mu operation. K and mu index pointwise problems;\allowbreak{} they are not joint asymptotic variables. Dependence of non-leading convergence thresholds on these fixed parameters is permitted;\allowbreak{} the retained leading coefficient is exactly T*(mu),\allowbreak{} with no hidden multiplier. No uniform convergence in K or mu is asserted.\par\endgroup
